Maintenance Report — MNT-0193-010

Asset: WELL-0193 (NE-08 Well 193, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 20 Jul 2024 08:00 · Finished: 06 Aug 2024 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 417 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0193-0091 on 2024-07-18 Report written: 08 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0193-0091 showed the wellhead at 42.2 °C with the air at 34.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil

Maintenance Report — MNT-0193-020

Asset: WELL-0193 (NE-08 Well 193, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 27 Mar 2026 08:00 · Finished: 27 Mar 2026 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 13 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0193-0177 on 2026-03-26 Report written: 28 Mar 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0193-0177 at 07:30 on 2026-03-26 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.8% of the pad area, estimated 2.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 350 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 280 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0193-020 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.8% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0193-023

Asset: WELL-0193 (NE-08 Well 193, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Aug 2026 08:00 · Finished: 08 Sep 2026 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 244 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0193-0199 on 2026-08-27 Report written: 08 Sep 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0193-0199 showed the wellhead at 42.9 °C with the air at 35.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 350 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 280 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0193-023 (WS-06).
